history.lessons: The verifier is over-collapsing to coarse semantic equivalence and missing state-changing side effects. The false positives suggest it is not strictly checking exact final DB state record-by-record, especially for: (1) toggle operations where parity/order matters and different combinations do not cancel to the same state, (2) tools with hidden side effects such as billing/charges, reservation/payment updates, cancellations, and full-record replacement semantics, (3) failed/invalid calls that cause no state change, and (4) cases where user-visible outcome also matters even if DB edits look similar. It also needs to treat generated ids/timestamps structurally rather than by literal value.

history.lessons: The verifier is over-crediting candidates when a side-effectful action seems irrelevant or is mentally treated like a harmless setting change. In these failures, telecom toggle tools and refuel/billing tools likely changed persistent device/line state or bill totals differently from GOLD, but the prompt did not force explicit accounting of every side effect and net parity of toggles. It also needs a stronger rule that extra successful side-effectful calls are FAIL even if the user goal sounds similar, and that billing/usage changes from refuel-like tools must be matched exactly.
